A later analysis of the same basins found large events increased by 25% at Andrews 1, 16% at Andrews 6 and 26% at Coyote 3 after 100% clear-cutting [ev_flood_hazard_jon00_1]. An FAO synthesis states that partial or complete removal of tree cover accelerates water discharge, increasing the risk of flood during the rainy season, and that for frequent rainfall events of short duration or low intensity forested soils may reduce or prevent flash floods locally [ev_flood_hazard_ham08_1, ev_flood_hazard_ham08_3]. At the local scale forests and forest soils reduce runoff through enhanced infiltration and storage, and peak flows rise after forest removal in small experimental catchments [ev_flood_hazard_faocifor05_1, ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_2]. A country-level analysis of developing countries predicted that a further hypothetical 10% loss of natural forest cover would raise flood frequency by 3.5% to 28.1% and flood duration by 3.8% to 7.9% [ev_flood_hazard_bradshaw07_1, ev_flood_hazard_bradshaw07_2]; in Malaysia an analysis with adequate controls for confounding factors found flood risk increased after natural forest was converted to plantation crops and urban land [ev_flood_hazard_iufro18_1]; and in Swiss valleys with more than 30% forest, snowmelt was more gradual and flooding risk lower [ev_flood_hazard_iufro18_2]. The WOCAT compiler for a protected learning site in Afghanistan rates flood impacts as decreased, with riverbanks revegetated [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_flood_impacts].
caveats: The harvest studies and the forest-loss analyses describe what existing forest does; they enter through the existing-forest comparator, which routes them to this protection family and keeps them out of the restoration families, so none of them is a restoration result. The Oregon large-basin increase is bundled with forest road construction and is stated as an upper bound, as much as [ev_flood_hazard_jg96_1]. The service fades with storm size and basin size. Complete clear-cutting without roads produced significant increases in fall and winter events but not for large events as a group [ev_flood_hazard_jg96_4], and at Andrews 10 large events did not change after 100% clear-cutting [ev_flood_hazard_jon00_2]. For the rarer prolonged or high-intensity storms, once the soil layer becomes saturated water will run off even where there is full, undisturbed forest cover [ev_flood_hazard_ham08_4]; forest soils reduce runoff only in small-scale rainfall events, which are not responsible for severe downstream flooding, and forests cannot stop catastrophic large-scale floods caused by severe meteorological events [ev_flood_hazard_faocifor05_1, ev_flood_hazard_faocifor05_2]; and small to medium peak flows are affected most while the largest events do not change noticeably [ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_3]. The cross-country analysis itself found little evidence that further forest loss changed flood deaths or damage [ev_flood_hazard_bradshaw07_3, ev_flood_hazard_bradshaw07_4], and a reanalysis found the correlation between forest cover or cover loss and flood frequency appears absent [ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_1].
